links.reason: Only the two words கவறு and கழகம் are shared, and the epic uses them as a figure for the woman's body, not as a gambling condemnation; the claim that the Kural's moral weight prepares the turn to restraint (ஆக நோற்றிட்டு அடங்கல்) is read in, not in the Tamil.

Verse 2679 answers 2678 by taking up her moon grievance: மதி உள்கறுத்துத் தேய்ந்தது முகவொளி எறிப்ப turns the paled-moon rival of 2678 into praise of her face, and he embraces her (புல்லினான்). The reversal of the sulk by the same conceit is stated in the Tamil.

Verse 81 has the father reason on the passing of youth and kin (இளமை, கிளைமை); verse 86 shows the prince turning to wealth and desire (அருத்த காமத் தறத்திற மறத்து). The contrast is real but the verses make no incompatible claim, and 'wisdom as personal, not inherited' is the note's gloss, not the Tamil.

Civakan's verse says only that sin from clinging to women (பசையினாற் பிறந்த பாவம்) cannot be washed by union with women; it says nothing about forest life or leaving the wife, so the 'shared attack on outward renunciation' and 'leaving the wife a condition' are read in. Pattinathar's வீடே இருப்பனும் beside women is a real contrast on household and release, but not a pairing of the same premise.

Kural 481 gives the crow beating the owl by the right time (பொழுது); 1927 opens இடத்தொடு பொழுது நாடி and tells of one crow among the owls in their own place (இடத்திடை) killing a thousand crore, adding place and judgment (மதிவல்லார்) to the couplet's time. That extension is stated in the Tamil.

Purananuru 219 names no Pisirandhaiyar and no fasting; it says only that many sat by your resolve (நின் குறிஇருந்தோர்), addressed to a warrior. The epic verse has Buddhisenan threatening kings and city (வாளினானே ... சவட்டிப் போகி), so the bridge to the sitting-fast tradition is carried by outside knowledge, not by either text.
links.text_issue: PN 219 sense flagged uncertain; epic verse repaired from 8 half-lines

links.reason: The Soolamani verse says there is no refuge but the austere sage's feet (செறிதவர் சரண ... அரண் பிறிதாவ துண்டோ) but never names Death; the Tirumanthiram verse is an invocation of Siva who kicked Death (கூற்றுதைத்தான்) and does not say only he shelters. The contrast of refuges is real, but 'refuge from Death' and 'reached by one's own austerity' come from the note.

In 176 the spring plants (மாந்தளிர், குயில்) take the women's colour and speech; in 451 the women's gait and feet confuse the peacock (மயிற்கண் மருட்டுவர் சாயல்). In both the women are the model, so 'the poet changes which side is the model' is false; the link is the common trope of nature matching women.

1547 proclaims the coronation for dawn (காலையா மணிவது) and 1550 has her crowned (பட்டங் கொண்டாள்), so the later verse fulfils the proclamation. But this is plot sequence, and 'the festival is a prelude, not decoration' is not shown by either verse.

1473 praises the king's rule (பூமி முழுதாண்டாய்) and 1481 asks why he left land and servants (பணித்த தென்னோ), both in the same lament in story order. The reproach is in 1481, but nothing in 1473 is answered or reversed, so this is sequence.

Lines 126-141 state ஆதி இல்லாப் பரமாணுக்கள் as the Ajivika's view (put to be answered); Sivavakkiyar's பூதமும் புலன்களும் அனாதிஅல்ல, ஆத்துமம் அனாதிஅல்ல denies beginninglessness of elements and soul and keeps it for the one truth. The incompatibility on whether the elements are beginningless is in the words; 'made' is a mild gloss on 'not beginningless'.

Verse 1573 has the jester say he will beat with his stick those who win by reciting (ஓதி வெல்லலுறுவார்களை); no gift or food is in the Tamil. Tirumanthiram 51 says the wise left debate (வாதத்தை விட்டு) and recited the Veda, so the jester attacks the very recitation the verse praises, and a farce is not a stated view that can be in tension.

The note rests on Kural 342 saying to renounce 'while there is time'; the Tamil வேண்டின் உண்டாகத் துறக்க has no word for time or urgency, and reads rather as renouncing so that what one wants comes about. The whole teaches (the Kural leaves 'time' open and the father fixes it) therefore reads in a sense the couplet lacks.

Epic 9 says only that the king and city were bewildered by wealth (செல்வ மயக்கினால்) and saw no road to release; it has no turtle or pot, so the shared image is only in the Naladiyar (ஆமை உலை ஏற்றி). The comparison of blinding comfort is real, but the 'consequence in a scene that follows' is not in the epic verse.
links.text_issue: epic 9 has no image of its own

links.reason: Kural 261 defines தவம் as bearing pain and not harming (உற்றநோய் நோன்றல், உயிர்க்கு உறுகண் செய்யாமை); epic 1547 uses தவமென்றார் for fasting on moon days and eighth day while keeping conduct (பட்டினி விட்டு ஒழுக்கம் காத்தல்). The same word is defined as an ethic and as a fixed practice, and the two readings add to each other.

In 2745 Civakan asks the sage's grace to drive off the dark of his deeds (இருள் விலங்க நின்றெரியும் நீள்சுடர் அருளும்); Tirumanthiram 114 reports Nandi cutting the tarnish (களிம்பறுத்தான்) and opening grace's eye. Both say a holy one's grace removes a stain, so no incompatible claim is shown; 'a teacher, not a god' is not in the epic verse.

3064 says Civakan's firm will (துப்பமை சிந்தையான்) cuts the eight karmas; Tirumanthiram 120 has the one who, like the swan, உடனே தாமே ... makes deeds into burnt seeds, and the reflexive தாமே points to the yogi himself, so nothing in the Tamil makes the burner a god or guru. The claimed tension rests on that reading and the two verses largely agree.

Kural 314 gives shaming by kindness (அவர்நாண நன்னயஞ் செய்து) for a personal injury and 550 gives the king's weeding out of the cruel (கொலையிற் கொடியாரை வேந்தொறுத்தல்). The shared word ஒறுத்தல் is the only link, and different advice for a person and a king is not a tension; 550 at most limits 314 to private wrongs.

1424 reports the deaths to the king and 1425 has him resolve on the spell (ஈங்கிவர் மாற்றமாயின் இருந்தினி என்னை), so the second is his reaction in plot order. 'The whole cause' of the spell is the note's gloss, and the pairing shows no reversal or answer beyond sequence.

883 does carry Civakan's resolve (கட்டியங்காரனைத் தோளை ஈர்ந்திடவே துணிவுற்ற வாள்) in a simile, and 2206 has a sky voice saying he will swallow Kattiyangaran's life. The echo of the purpose is real, but 'planted aside' and 'public fulfilment' are the note's reading; 2206 is a proclamation, not the fulfilment.

YK72 sums a denial of rebirth and of two deeds (இரு வினை தானு மில்லென்று) and calls it ignorance; Neelakesi 859 is the elements-only claim (உலகெலாம் அவையே) against talk of a soul. Both are the materialist side but the claims differ, so 'the same opponent' is a stretch and develops does not fit.

2009 says to melt for another's life as for one's own (ஓருயிர் போல உருகி) and, where help fails, keep a moist heart (நெஞ்சகத் தீர முடைமை அருளின் இயல்பே); Kural 315 says knowledge is useless without guarding another's pain as one's own. The epic adds a stated allowance for failure that the couplet does not give.

2590 has Anangamalai ask whether she is outside the umbrella that is the shade of dharma (அறனிழலாய் ... வெண்குடை), and Purananuru 35 says the umbrella is not for shade but to cover the suffering subjects (குடிமறைப்பதுவே). The umbrella image is shared, but her petition over her friend does not test PN35's claim, and nothing shows the epic invokes it.
links.text_issue: 2590 repaired from 8 half-lines; sense flagged uncertain

links.reason: Visakai's lines 135-138 (இளமையும் நில்லாது ... மிக்க அறமே விழுத் துணை) share the idea of virtue as the lasting companion with Kural 36 (பொன்றாக் துணை). But the unit says nothing of a brahmin demanding a wife or of marriage for heaven, so the 'answer to that claim' is read in from outside the Tamil.

1183 describes women who embrace and wring out a man's life (புல்லலும் பிழிந்துயிர் உண்டிடும் பேய்கள்); Kural 918 calls the embrace of deceiving women an அணங்கு to the undiscerning. The matching is real, but அணங்கு is itself a being, so 'hyperbole' is not shown, and the god's forewarning standing for discerning sense is an added reading.

The only link is the number five: Kural 343's ஐந்தன் புலத்தை are the senses, and 2109's ஐவர் படைத் தலைவர் are the five vows (விரத நோன்மைப் படை). The note itself says they are different disciplines, so the pairing is a shared number dressed as a qualification.

1743 calls the teachers பொய்யாக் கல்விச் செல்வர் and Kural 400 calls learning கேடில் விழுச்செல்வம்; the only shared words are கல்வி and செல்வம், not a run of four. The verse does not show the king's other wealth beside it, so the 'test of whether learning is the only wealth' is added.

Verse 132 says only that the king, meaning to give up the kingdom, bows to his mother, who blesses a long reign; no disenchantment, wife or loss is in the Tamil. The link depends on the reconstructed story to supply the grief and betrayal, and Siddhar 249's list of what is not lasting is then only illustrated.

3044 only has Senikan order a feast for the Jina's feet (திருவடி விருந்து செய்வான்); no reward or merit is mentioned, and 'the fruit the next lines tell' is outside the verse. Purananuru 134 (அறவிலை வணிகன்) refuses giving for the next birth, so the epic verse offers nothing to set against it.

Verse 7 praises Saccandan's unbending sceptre (கோடாத செங்கோல்); 2372 has Civakan bid his brother clear the towns' afflictions, and it does not say it is his first act or that it repairs a wrong. The 'repair of the wrong the story began with' is the note's reconstruction, not either text.

742 has Kattiyankaran taunt beaten kings to give up crowns for the hermit forest (முடிதுறந் தளியிர் போகி முனிவனம் புகுமின்); 27 has Civakan hear the dharma and renounce at the height of his rule (அரசு அஞ்சித் துறந்த). The later reverses the sense of renunciation, but the two do not claim incompatible things about one subject, and 'staged contempt the book will overturn' is the note's intent.

139 has the king say kings are the shield of living things (மன்னுயிர்க் கரண மண்மேல் மன்னவர்); 209 has a king in rage seize the merchants' goods and the buffalo. Nothing in the Tamil says the 209 king is the successor of the 139 king, so a claim and a refuting scene is not shown; it is a contrast of two rulers.

Ainkurunuru 256 says the girl, though young (இளையள் ஆயினும்), is a striking power (ஆர் அணங்கினளே); Kural 1081 asks whether the woman is அணங்கு, peahen or woman. The word shared is real, but Ainkurunuru does not ask the question, and 'refinement of an older certainty' is a claim about priority the texts do not show.

458 has men say the women's eyes are skilled at killing (நெடுங்கண் இவை வல்லகொலை); Kural 1085 asks whether the look is Death, an eye or a doe. The eye-as-killer trope is shared, but the Kural does not state 'the look is Death', and the 'crowd of men' gain is trivial.

291 has the king, having fought (மறமும் ஆற்றி) and bearing the Jina's feet and mantra-sandal, become விண்ணோர்க்கு விருந்து; Puram 62 ends with the gods receiving guests (விருந்துபெற்றனரால்). The added Jina devotion is true, but PN62's kings fought மறப்போர் ... அறத்தின் மண்டிய, so heaven is not 'in fighting alone', and the 'negligent king' is not in 291.

2513 has the parrot's mock hanging make her laugh, and Civakan embrace her; his earlier yielding is not in this verse, so 'yielding does not by itself end the sulk' is supplied by the note. Kural 1327 says the loser wins in the union, and the verse's வரம்பெற்றேன் is a thin echo, so no limit on the rule is shown.

3121 has the women reach heaven as Indras (இந்திரர்களாய்த் துறக்கம் எய்தினார்); Kural 346 says one who cuts off 'I' and 'mine' enters a world higher than the gods' (வானோர்க்கு உயர்ந்த உலகம்). The epic does not say heaven is a stop or that more lies above it, so the tension needs a Jain-ladder reading the verse does not state.

948 shows the dog reborn as a god, and 15 says a god came down the sky like lightning and carried Civakan out of prison. The Tamil of 15 does not say it is that god or tie it to a kindness at the festival, so the cause-and-return is supplied from the story, not from the verses.

1366 has the chief mount and frighten all (எவரும் அஞ்ச), and 1381 has the Vidyadharas turn back in fear of fate-marked men (விதிபடு மனிசரை வெருவி). 1381 gives fate, not the rider's terror, as the cause, so the note's causal chain is read in and the pair is sequence.

1509 has Kemasari say her life strains to leave (ஆருயிர் ஈண்டு உடம்பு ஒழித்தேக வலிக்கும்), and 1530 has her hold back the leaving life (ஆவி தாங்கினள்) out of fear for her husband (கேள்வற்கு ஊனமும் பிரிவும் அஞ்சி). The second answers and reverses the first, which fits develops, not tension, and the 'not his return but her fear' reading is in the Tamil.

Dharmadattan tells Kattiyankaran that seizing the king who raised him (தன்னை ஆக்கிய ... வேந்தனை வௌவில்) makes Fortune turn from him, and loyalty secures his line (தன் குலம் பேர்க்குநர் இல்லை). Kural 110's no-escape for one who kills a benefit (செய்ந்நன்றி கொன்ற) is given a worldly form of loss of fortune and line, offered as counsel to a usurper.

2875 has caged birds torn from kin and warns that their keepers will be parted from their own (தங்கிளையின் நீங்கிப் போவர்); Naladiyar 122 says those who cage partridges and quails will go in irons as slaves to strangers. The same crime meeting two repayments is true and specific, but neither extends the other, so agrees fits better than develops.

UKK 257 has prince and girl both bewildered by love's arrow (இருவரும் மயக்கமுற்று) and united at once; Kural 1081 is a man's doubt whether she is அணங்கு, peahen or woman, with no shared words beyond the theme of first sight. The 'path to union' and 'doubt never has time to arise' are the note's reading of a conventional love-at-sight verse.
